subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bounded provider-normalized tool-schema cache now for bundled provider compat helpers, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The source path confirms repeated normalization remains, but cache scope and invalidation are provider/runtime lifecycle decisions that should not be picked by cleanup automation while an open PR and broader migration both exist.

options.title: Land the bounded cache after review
options.body: Resolve the open PR's dirty state and require proof that bundled helpers cache safely while custom provider hooks bypass the cache.

options.title: Fold into prepared-runtime migration
options.body: Keep this issue open under the broader prepared-runtime tracking work if maintainers want one canonical runtime-fact solution instead of a focused cache.

options.title: Reject core cache for now
options.body: Leave the behavior to provider/plugin-specific mitigation only if maintainers decide schema freshness outweighs the reported performance and provider-ban risk.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded cache after review
recommendation.body: Resolve the open PR's dirty state and require proof that bundled helpers cache safely while custom provider hooks bypass the cache.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent provider/runtime and release history makes vincentkoc the strongest routing candidate for the cache lifecycle decision.
